statement: For step reliability p=0.70 across k=5 trials, pass^5 = 0.70^5 = 0.16807 (16.81%), exposing the common slide-deck exponentiation pitfall that confuses 0.7^5 with 0.75.
sample_size_or_bounds: k=5 trials; exact closed-form bound [0.16807, 0.16807]
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes independent identically distributed (i.i.d.) step success Bernoulli trials.

statement: For a single-step success rate p_step=0.95 across an m=10 step sequential workflow, single-trajectory success is 0.95^10 = 0.5987, and 5-run consecutive dependability pass^5 is (0.95^10)^5 = 0.0769 (7.69%), while optimistic pass@5 is 1 - (1 - 0.5987)^5 = 0.9896 (98.96%).
sample_size_or_bounds: m=10 steps, k=5 trials; analytical bounds
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes independent steps; under-represents failure risk if errors correlate across steps.

statement: Because g(p) = 1 - (1-p)^k is strictly concave on [0,1] for k>1 (g''(p) = -k(k-1)(1-p)^{k-2} < 0), Jensen's inequality proves the naive plug-in estimator 1 - (1-c/n)^k is negatively biased (biased downward, e.g., -0.125 at p=0.5, n=2, k=2), whereas the Chen et al. (2021) hypergeometric estimator 1 - C(n-c, k)/C(n, k) is strictly unbiased.
sample_size_or_bounds: n=2 to 100 items, k=2 to 10 evaluations; analytical proof + N=10,000 Monte Carlo check
seed_and_deterministic_params: Analytical proof; PRNG seed=2026 for simulation confirmation
assumptions_and_limits: Valid for any n >= k; Chen hypergeometric estimator assumes sampling without replacement from n evaluation items.

statement: Under Beta(alpha, beta) task difficulty heterogeneity, the marginal k-trial dependability E[P^k] = B(alpha+k, beta)/B(alpha, beta) strictly exceeds the naive plug-in power (E[P])^k by Jensen's inequality for convex functions on [0,1].
sample_size_or_bounds: alpha, beta > 0; k >= 2; analytical moments + N=5,000 synthetic tasks
seed_and_deterministic_params: Analytical proof via Jensen; seed=2026 for Beta draws
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes task difficulty follows Beta distribution; holds for any non-degenerate prior variance sigma^2 > 0.

statement: Positive Markov step correlation (where an early step error degrades subsequent context transitions) increases trajectory failure variance and creates bimodal all-or-nothing execution outcomes.
sample_size_or_bounds: N=10,000 simulated trajectories, m=10 steps, transition matrix P(step_t+1 | step_t)
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes first-order Markov memory; higher-order context compounding further amplifies bimodality.

statement: For m=20 independent steps at p_step=0.98, single-run trajectory completion is 0.98^20 = 0.6676, and 10-batch consecutive completion pass^10 drops to 0.0176 (1.76%).
sample_size_or_bounds: m=20 steps, k=10 consecutive runs; analytical exact
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes step independence; demonstrates why demo reliability does not scale to multi-turn agents.

statement: On a 50-prompt demo with 48 successes (p_hat = 0.9600), the two-sided 95% Wilson score confidence interval is [0.8654, 0.9890], proving the true accuracy can be as low as 86.5%.
sample_size_or_bounds: N=50 trials, k=48 successes; 95% Wilson CI [0.8654, 0.9890]
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes exchangeable test items; valid for small sample sizes where Wald intervals fail.

statement: When k=0 failures are observed in n independent trials, the exact one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound is U_0.95 = 1 - 0.05^(1/n) approx 3/n (Rule of Three); certifying <1.0% failure rate at 95% confidence requires n >= 299 trials.
sample_size_or_bounds: n=299 trials (k=0); exact one-sided upper bound U_0.95 = 0.00995 < 0.0100
seed_and_deterministic_params: Exact Clopper-Pearson binomial tail bisection (tolerance eps=1e-7)
assumptions_and_limits: Exact conservative coverage >= 1 - alpha under arbitrary true proportion p in [0, 1].

statement: The naive Wald interval p_hat +/- z*sqrt(p_hat*(1-p_hat)/n) collapses to zero width [1.0, 1.0] at k=n and suffers severe empirical under-coverage near p in {0.95, 0.99}.
sample_size_or_bounds: n in [10, 100], N=10,000 Monte Carlo coverage experiments
assumptions_and_limits: Wald interval requires asymptotic normality; invalidated near parameter boundaries.

statement: On a 25-prompt red-team audit with 0 observed failures, the exact 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound on true failure rate is 1 - 0.05^(1/25) = 11.29%.
sample_size_or_bounds: n=25 trials, k=0 failures; exact bound U_0.95 = 0.1129
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes independent adversarial probes; highlights danger of declaring zero-vulnerability on small audits.

statement: Agresti-Coull ('add 2 successes and 2 failures') shifts the binomial center toward 0.5 by z^2/2, preventing boundary degeneracy at small n.
sample_size_or_bounds: Analytical formulation for arbitrary n and k; tested across n in [5, 500]
assumptions_and_limits: Approximates Wilson center while retaining simple Wald-like formulation.

statement: Cohen's arcsine transformation h = 2*arcsin(sqrt(p1)) - 2*arcsin(sqrt(p2)) stabilizes binomial variance to 1/n regardless of baseline proportion p.
sample_size_or_bounds: Analytical derivation + power calculation for Delta in [0.05, 0.20]
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes normal approximation on arcsine-root scale; valid for sample sizing.

statement: In paired evaluation of Model A vs. Model B on identical items, the variance of the paired difference Var(p_hat_A - p_hat_B) = (b + c - (b-c)^2/n)/n^2 depends only on discordant counts (b, c), reducing required sample size by 3x-5x under positive item correlation rho >= 0.70.
sample_size_or_bounds: N=200 items, correlation rho in [0.50, 0.85]; analytical variance identity
assumptions_and_limits: Requires identical item test sets for both models; assumes paired bivariate Bernoulli trials.

statement: At N=200 items with baseline p_A=0.80, candidate p_B=0.86, and item correlation rho=0.72, paired McNemar testing achieves >80% (approx 82.2%) statistical power whereas unpaired two-proportion testing achieves <30% (approx 25.7%) power, demonstrating a >3x power efficiency advantage.
sample_size_or_bounds: N=200 items, 10,000 simulated paired evaluation sweeps; paired power 82.2% vs unpaired 25.7%
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes positive item correlation typical in LLM benchmark items; validates paired evaluation protocol.

statement: Bowker's test of internal symmetry generalizes McNemar's test to K x K graded rubrics via chi^2 = sum_{i<j} (n_{ij} - n_{ji})^2 / (n_{ij} + n_{ji}) with K(K-1)/2 degrees of freedom.
sample_size_or_bounds: K=3 to 5 ordinal grades, N=300 paired evaluations
assumptions_and_limits: Requires sufficient expected discordant counts in off-diagonal cells.

statement: Cochran's Q statistic tests marginal homogeneity across M >= 3 matched prompt or model treatments on N binary items.
sample_size_or_bounds: M=4 model treatments, N=150 matched items
seed_and_deterministic_params: Analytical Q test derivation with chi^2(M-1) distribution
assumptions_and_limits: Requires matched binary outcomes across all treatments.

statement: The step-down Holm-Bonferroni procedure controls Family-Wise Error Rate (FWER <= alpha) under arbitrary dependence across M comparisons while remaining uniformly more powerful than classical Bonferroni alpha/M.
sample_size_or_bounds: M=10 candidate prompt sweeps; analytical p-value adjustment
seed_and_deterministic_params: Closed-form sequential sorting and multiplier array
assumptions_and_limits: Proof holds under arbitrary dependence structure; uniformly more powerful than standard Bonferroni.

statement: Multi-factor ANOVA variance decomposition isolates item difficulty variance sigma_item^2 from decoding temperature seed variance sigma_seed^2 and judge variance sigma_judge^2.
sample_size_or_bounds: N=50 items x 5 seeds x 3 judges = 750 factorial evaluations
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes linear additive component model with homoscedastic residual variance.

statement: Selecting the best of M independent prompt/hyperparameter configurations on a finite test set of size N without multiple-testing correction inflates the Family-Wise Error Rate to 1 - (1 - alpha)^M (e.g., 40.1% false-positive rate at M=10, alpha=0.05).
verification_source: Extreme value order statistics & Šidák identity
sample_size_or_bounds: M=10 configurations, alpha=0.05; exact identity 1 - 0.95^10 = 0.4013
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes independent evaluation trials across candidates; lower bound for dependent candidates.

statement: The expected maximum of M independent standard normal noise draws scales asymptotically as sqrt(2*ln(M)), creating systematic selection optimism Delta_leak on over-queried validation splits.
sample_size_or_bounds: M in [10, 1000]; extreme value limit compared against N=10,000 draws
assumptions_and_limits: Asymptotic convergence for independent Gaussian noise perturbations.

statement: Applying synthetic oversampling or global feature/embedding normalization prior to group-temporal train/test splitting leaks test manifold geometry, inflating apparent evaluation accuracy by >20 percentage points over leak-proof group-time splits.
sample_size_or_bounds: N=1,000 synthetic items, 80/20 train/test split, 100 Monte Carlo trials
assumptions_and_limits: Demonstrates pipeline leakage where test fold statistics inform preprocessing.

statement: Shingled character/token n-gram Jaccard and MinHash containment scanning detects verbatim and paraphrased benchmark leakage between training corpora and evaluation holdouts.
sample_size_or_bounds: 5-gram and 8-gram shingles, 128 MinHash permutations over 500 test items
assumptions_and_limits: Detects syntactic token containment; semantic paraphrasing requires counterfactual perturbation.

statement: Splitting multi-turn agent logs randomly by message rather than grouped by user_id/entity_id leaks entity-specific context across train and test sets.
sample_size_or_bounds: 250 user sessions, 1,500 messages; grouped vs ungrouped split
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes intra-session correlation typical in enterprise customer service dialogues.

statement: Point-in-time look-ahead leakage occurs when retrieval indices or features incorporate post-decision dispute flags or document edits dated after t_decision.
sample_size_or_bounds: 500 historical dispute cases with temporal timestamps t_event < t_eval < t_resolution
assumptions_and_limits: Demonstrates retroactive data contamination in RAG retrieval indexes.

statement: Grading tool-using agents by verbal completion claims rather than out-of-band point-in-time relational state diffs and double-entry ledger invariants produces a >20% False Victory rate when partial tool failures or collateral mutations occur.
sample_size_or_bounds: N=200 simulated agent tool-call execution trajectories
assumptions_and_limits: Derived from composite incident INC-2026-01 (silent partial tool write failures).

statement: In a double-entry financial ledger state oracle, any valid state transition S_0 -> S_final must preserve the conservation invariant sum(debits) - sum(credits) == 0 across all accounts.
sample_size_or_bounds: 100 multi-account ledger transactions; exact integer balance check
assumptions_and_limits: Exact algebraic invariant; violation flags unhandled exception or non-atomic transaction.

statement: Bi-temporal point-in-time state queries (valid_from <= t_eval AND recorded_at <= t_eval) prevent hindsight contamination during historical agent replay.
sample_size_or_bounds: 1,000 historical ledger states across 50 simulated business days
assumptions_and_limits: Requires immutable append-only event log or bi-temporal snapshot tables.

statement: Collateral side-effect verification hashes all non-target rows (e not in E_target) before and after agent execution to guarantee zero unintended deletions or updates.
sample_size_or_bounds: 500 non-target database rows, SHA-256 canonical state hash
assumptions_and_limits: Detects broad table updates, stray DELETE queries, or collateral trigger activations.

statement: Given an automated judge with sensitivity q1 and specificity q0 (Youden's J = q1 + q0 - 1 > 0), the raw observed pass rate p_obs = p*q1 + (1-p)*(1-q0) is inverted via the Rogan-Gladen estimator p_hat = clip_[0,1]((p_obs + q0 - 1)/(q1 + q0 - 1)).
sample_size_or_bounds: Analytical prevalence inversion; verified across p in [0.05, 0.95]
assumptions_and_limits: Requires Youden index J = q1 + q0 - 1 > 0; assumes stationary judge error rates.

statement: The first-order multivariate delta-method variance of the Rogan-Gladen estimator is Var(p_hat) = (1/J^2)*[p_obs*(1-p_obs)/n_eval + p_hat^2*q1*(1-q1)/m1 + (1-p_hat)^2*q0*(1-q0)/m0], proving that finite calibration sets (m1, m0) bound achievable precision.
verification_source: Multivariate Taylor expansion proof (Ch06 & App C)
sample_size_or_bounds: m1=150, m0=150 calibration items, n_eval=500; analytical covariance expansion
assumptions_and_limits: First-order asymptotic approximation; valid when m1, m0 >= 100 and J >= 0.40.

statement: An uncalibrated LLM judge with sensitivity q1=0.88 and specificity q0=0.76 inflates a true 60.0% pass rate to an observed 62.4% and distorts extreme pass rates by up to 14+ percentage points before Rogan-Gladen correction.
sample_size_or_bounds: N=10,000 simulated judge evaluations across grid p in [0.05, 0.95]
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes constant misclassification probabilities across prompt difficulties.

statement: As Youden's index J = q1 + q0 - 1 approaches 0, the variance inflation factor 1/J^2 diverges to infinity, proving a noisy judge cannot be rescued simply by running more uncalibrated evaluations n_eval.
sample_size_or_bounds: J in [0.01, 1.0]; analytical singularity limit
assumptions_and_limits: Proves uncalibrated or near-chance judges cannot be rescued by increasing n_eval.

statement: Bidirectional position-swapping (evaluating both (A,B) and (B,A) orders) isolates positional primacy/recency bias Delta_pos and quarantines inconsistent judge verdicts.
sample_size_or_bounds: N=300 pairwise model comparisons evaluated in both (A,B) and (B,A) orders
assumptions_and_limits: Eliminates first-mover advantage; assumes order inversion leaves true content unchanged.

statement: Sequential Elo ratings depend on chronological match ordering and swing by +/-30 to 50 Elo points under random match permutations on a fixed win matrix, whereas Bradley-Terry-Davidson MLE via Zermelo MM updates is strictly order-invariant.
sample_size_or_bounds: 1,000 match ordering permutations over 8 competing LLMs (2,000 matches)
seed_and_deterministic_params: random.Random(2026), Zermelo MM solver tolerance eps=1e-8
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes underlying transitive latent strength vector pi; highlights Elo order path-dependency.

statement: In the Davidson (1970) extension of the Bradley-Terry model, tie probability is modeled as P(i approx j) = nu*sqrt(pi_i*pi_j) / (pi_i + pi_j + nu*sqrt(pi_i*pi_j)), preserving log-likelihood concavity.
sample_size_or_bounds: Analytical Hessian proof; verified on N=500 matches with 25% ties
assumptions_and_limits: Strictly concave objective function guarantees unique global maximum.

statement: Pairwise preference matrices across multi-objective AI tasks (coding, safety, conciseness) can exhibit non-transitive Condorcet cycles (A > B > C > A) detectable via curl/cycle residuals that violate scalar Elo/BTL assumptions.
sample_size_or_bounds: 3-model triad with 600 simulated pairwise votes; cycle intensity curl > 0.15
assumptions_and_limits: Violates 1D scalar ranking assumptions when models excel on orthogonal dimensions.

statement: Explicitly modeling first-position advantage gamma in pairwise arena log-likelihood strips order bias from latent model skill estimates pi_i.
sample_size_or_bounds: N=1,200 arena matches with 12% first-position preference bias
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes position advantage is multiplicative and homogeneous across pairings.

statement: Decomposing RAG evaluation into Retrieval (Recall@K, MRR, NDCG@K) and Generation Grounding (atomic claim entailment, citation precision, negative rejection) isolates retrieval misses from generator hallucinations that end-to-end scores conflate.
sample_size_or_bounds: N=250 RAG queries across 1,000 document chunks
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes gold retrieval relevance judgments and atomic claim decomposition.

statement: Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain NDCG@K = DCG@K / IDCG@K with DCG@K = sum_{i=1}^K (2^{rel_i} - 1)/log2(i+1) weights top-ranked relevant chunks logarithmically and lies strictly in [0, 1].
sample_size_or_bounds: K in [3, 10], graded relevance rel in {0, 1, 2, 3}; analytical bounds
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes non-negative relevance gains; normalized against ideal ranking IDCG.

statement: Citation verification must audit both claim faithfulness (is the claim entailed by the context?) and citation precision (does the specific cited chunk [doc_k] actually support the claim?).
sample_size_or_bounds: 150 generated responses with 450 cited chunk references
seed_and_deterministic_params: Deterministic sentence splitter and citation token parser
assumptions_and_limits: Evaluates atomic chunk entailment; catches hallucinated citation tags.

statement: Long-context compaction and 'lost-in-the-middle' position decay degrade retrieval and safety constraint survival for facts positioned near relative depth d in [0.4, 0.6].
sample_size_or_bounds: 100 long-context prompts (32k tokens) with needle planted at depths 0.0 to 1.0
assumptions_and_limits: Reproduces 'lost-in-the-middle' attention decay documented in literature.

statement: Evaluating trajectories via the 2x2 Outcome-Trajectory matrix and loop-cycle entropy detects 'Lucky Guess / Unsafe Shortcut' runs that pass final output checks while executing redundant or oscillatory tool calls.
sample_size_or_bounds: N=200 agent task executions; 2x2 classification (Safe-Success, Unsafe-Success, Clean-Fail, Chaotic-Fail)
assumptions_and_limits: Derived from composite incident INC-2026-03 (production agent looping and bill runaway).

statement: Step Optimality Ratio eta_steps = L_opt / L_actual in (0, 1] measures trajectory path efficiency relative to the shortest valid tool execution DAG.
sample_size_or_bounds: DAG lengths L_opt in [3, 8], actual steps up to 25; analytical ratio
assumptions_and_limits: Requires pre-defined valid dependency DAG for the target goal.

statement: Transition bigram repetition and sliding-window Shannon entropy over (tool, args_hash) sequences deterministically detect A -> B -> A agent oscillation loops before max_steps exhaustion.
sample_size_or_bounds: 50 oscillating agent trajectories; window size w=6 steps
seed_and_deterministic_params: Exact Shannon entropy calculator: H = -sum(p * log2(p))
assumptions_and_limits: Detects stationary repetitive cycles; does not catch non-repeating divergent drift.

statement: In an M-step sequential agent where each step has independent P99 tail latency survival 0.99, the probability that a workflow experiences at least one P99 tail stall is 1 - 0.99^M (9.56% at M=10, 18.21% at M=20).
sample_size_or_bounds: M in [1, 50] steps, step survival p_tail=0.99; analytical exact
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes independent step latencies; correlated network congestions further increase tail stall risk.

statement: Accumulating conversation history of Delta_L tokens per step across M agent turns without prefix KV-caching incurs quadratic total input token cost M*L_0 + M*(M+1)/2 * Delta_L.
sample_size_or_bounds: M in [1, 30] turns, L_0=500, Delta_L=300 tokens; exact series summation
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes uncompacted context; mitigated by prompt caching or rolling window compaction.

statement: Effective Cost per Verified Task (ECVT) divides total expected run cost (tokens + tools + human escalation + incident remediation) by consecutive reliability pass^k, exposing the true unit economics of unreliable agents.
sample_size_or_bounds: Base cost $0.05, remediation $5.00, pass rate p=0.80, k=5 runs; ECVT calculation
assumptions_and_limits: Formalizes true enterprise cost of low-reliability demo agents.

statement: Fenton-Wilkinson moment matching approximates the sum of M independent Log-Normal step latencies across multi-step agent trajectories.
sample_size_or_bounds: M=10 steps, mu=2.0, sigma=0.6; compared against N=10,000 Monte Carlo draws
assumptions_and_limits: Valid for moderate skewness; extreme heavy-tail Pareto latencies require generalized extreme value bounds.

statement: Injecting seeded HTTP 429/503 faults, ambiguous post-commit timeouts, and schema drift into an unhardened ReAct loop causes non-idempotent duplicate writes and retry amplification (>2x), whereas an idempotency-and-circuit-breaker harness maintains 0.00% silent state corruption.
sample_size_or_bounds: N=100 simulated network chaos scenarios, 30% fault injection rate
assumptions_and_limits: Derived from composite incident INC-2026-02 (payment gateway retry cascade).

statement: Ambiguous post-commit timeouts (where the server commits a state mutation before the network response drops) cause duplicate financial side effects unless guarded by deterministic idempotency keys.
sample_size_or_bounds: 50 post-commit drop events; verified duplicate write count (unguarded: 50, guarded: 0)
assumptions_and_limits: Demonstrates distributed systems two-generals failure mode in LLM tool calling.

statement: Returning HTTP 200 OK with an upstream HTML error page or renamed JSON keys triggers hallucinated fallback arguments in unguarded agents unless blocked by strict schema validation.
sample_size_or_bounds: 40 schema drift fault scenarios; structural validation assertions
assumptions_and_limits: Demonstrates failure of unvalidated string parsing on upstream API drift.

statement: Planting cryptographic canary tokens (CANARY-UUID-HMAC) in restricted records provides a deterministic 0%-false-positive oracle for indirect prompt injection exfiltration across tool calls and markdown links.
sample_size_or_bounds: 100 simulated exfiltration attempts across markdown, tool args, and HTTP queries
assumptions_and_limits: Deterministic substring match; zero false positives on benign untainted sessions.

statement: Evaluating security guardrails solely on Attack Success Rate (ASR) without measuring False Refusal Rate (FRR) on benign look-alike queries conceals degenerate 'refuse-everything' filters.
sample_size_or_bounds: 200 adversarial queries + 200 benign look-alike queries; ROC operating point
assumptions_and_limits: Standard signal detection theory applied to LLM safety guardrails.

statement: Stratified adversarial evaluation across OWASP Agentic Security categories (ASI01-ASI10) exposes multi-step privilege escalation and memory poisoning missed by single-turn jailbreak lists.
sample_size_or_bounds: 10 OWASP risk categories, 20 test vectors per category (200 total)
assumptions_and_limits: Derived from composite incident INC-2026-04 (multi-hop tool privilege escalation).

statement: Cohen's kappa = (p_o - p_e)/(1 - p_e) corrects raw two-rater percent agreement p_o for chance agreement p_e, preventing inflated inter-annotator reliability claims on skewed class distributions.
sample_size_or_bounds: N=200 double-annotated items, class balance 90/10; analytical calculation
seed_and_deterministic_params: Closed-form Cohen (1960) formula: kappa = (p_o - p_e)/(1 - p_e)
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes two fixed raters evaluating nominal categories; sensitive to marginal prevalence.

statement: Fleiss' kappa generalizes chance-corrected inter-rater agreement to M >= 3 raters over N items, and Krippendorff's alpha handles missing ratings and ordinal/interval distance metrics.
sample_size_or_bounds: M=5 raters, N=100 items, 10% missing ratings; analytical matrix algebra
seed_and_deterministic_params: Closed-form coincidence matrix and disagreement calculation
assumptions_and_limits: Alpha is metric-independent and naturally handles missing data.

statement: The Dawid-Skene Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm estimates individual annotator confusion matrices and recovers latent gold truth with >4x lower label error than naive majority voting when raters have heterogeneous skill.
sample_size_or_bounds: M=7 annotators, N=300 items, error rates varying from 0.05 to 0.40
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes conditional independence of annotator ratings given latent class.

statement: Under the Pollaczek-Khinchine M/G/1 queueing formula W_q = lambda*(sigma_s^2 + 1/mu^2)/(2*(1-rho)), mean human review wait time diverges to infinity as reviewer utilization rho = lambda/mu approaches 1, accelerating cognitive fatigue errors.
sample_size_or_bounds: lambda in [0.1, 0.95], service time mean 1.0, cv in [0.5, 2.0]; analytical queue
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes Poisson arrivals and general stationary service time distribution.

statement: Population Stability Index PSI = sum (P_b - Q_b)*ln(P_b/Q_b) is mathematically identical to symmetric Jeffreys divergence J(P, Q) = D_KL(P||Q) + D_KL(Q||P) and is non-negative, vanishing if and only if P_b = Q_b for all bins.
sample_size_or_bounds: B=10 bins; analytical divergence identity; verified on drifted distributions
seed_and_deterministic_params: Closed-form Jeffreys divergence: sum((P_b - Q_b) * ln(P_b / Q_b))
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes non-zero bin counts (regularized via Laplace epsilon=1e-4).

statement: The exact 1D 1-Wasserstein (Earth Mover's) distance between empirical distributions X and Y of equal size n equals the L1 distance between their sorted order statistics: (1/n)*sum |X_(i) - Y_(i)|.
sample_size_or_bounds: n=500 samples; exact sorted absolute difference: (1/n)*sum(|X_(i) - Y_(i)|)
seed_and_deterministic_params: Exact Vallender (1974) sorting formulation (no optimization required)
assumptions_and_limits: Analytical theorem holds strictly in one dimension on the real line.

statement: Page's tabular CUSUM control chart detects sustained small shifts (1-2 sigma) in production oracle pass rates significantly faster than static daily threshold alerts.
sample_size_or_bounds: 30 daily batches (N=100 per day), step shift introduced at day 15
assumptions_and_limits: Optimal for detecting persistent mean shifts under known in-control distribution.

statement: Jensen-Shannon Divergence JSD(P || Q) = 0.5*D_KL(P || M) + 0.5*D_KL(Q || M) with M = 0.5*(P+Q) is symmetric and strictly bounded in [0, ln(2)] (or [0, 1] in base 2) even when support bins have zero counts.
sample_size_or_bounds: B=20 bins; analytical bounds [0.0, 1.0] (base 2); tested across extreme distributions
seed_and_deterministic_params: Closed-form mixture midpoint formulation: M = 0.5*(P + Q)
assumptions_and_limits: Finite and well-defined across arbitrary probability measures with overlapping support.

statement: Chaining telemetry records via H_i = SHA256(H_{i-1} || canonical_json(e_i)) guarantees cryptographic tamper-evidence: any post-hoc modification or deletion of event e_k invalidates all subsequent hashes H_m for m >= k.
sample_size_or_bounds: Chain of 100 historical telemetry events; single bit modification test
seed_and_deterministic_params: hashlib.sha256 with canonical RFC 8785 JSON serialization
assumptions_and_limits: Security relies on SHA-256 second preimage and collision resistance.

statement: Deterministic PII/secret scrubbing prior to hash-chain ingestion preserves cryptographic auditability while preventing sensitive credentials from persisting in immutable telemetry stores.
sample_size_or_bounds: 50 telemetry events containing API keys, emails, and credit card patterns
seed_and_deterministic_params: Deterministic regex scrubbing filter (canonical replacement tokens)
assumptions_and_limits: Scrubbing must be performed synchronously before hashing to ensure hash chain validity.

statement: Freezing production incident tool responses into content-addressed replay cassettes enables deterministic CI/CD verification of gateway fixes without re-invoking live external APIs.
sample_size_or_bounds: 10 production incident cassettes (INC-2026-01 to INC-2026-05)
seed_and_deterministic_params: SHA-256 cassette address and deterministic HTTP mock proxy
assumptions_and_limits: Assumes isolated mock playback; prevents external network flakes in CI regression suites.

statement: Enforcing the 6-tuple ReleaseBundleManifest and 4-Stage EvaluationReleaseGate programmatically blocks underpowered red-team runs, uncalibrated judge inflation, chaos corruption, and reviewer queue overload before production deployment.
sample_size_or_bounds: 20 candidate release bundles evaluated against 4 sequential gating stages
assumptions_and_limits: Gate fails fast at earliest violating stage, conserving evaluation compute.

statement: Binding (model_digest, system_prompt_sha256, tool_registry_sha256, decoding_config_sha256, eval_dataset_sha256, oracle_suite_sha256) into a composite SHA-256 manifest ensures that any change to any component invalidates stale evaluation sign-offs.
sample_size_or_bounds: 6-tuple cryptographic digest; 1-character mutation test across each component
assumptions_and_limits: Guarantees end-to-end immutability across model, prompt, dataset, and code changes.

statement: The Unified FailMetry Engine integrates Wilson/Clopper-Pearson bounds, paired McNemar tests, Rogan-Gladen calibration, state-mutation oracles, pass@k vs pass^k, PSI drift, and 4-stage release gating in a single zero-dependency executable.
sample_size_or_bounds: End-to-end unified test suite covering all 16 chapter algorithms
seed_and_deterministic_params: Deterministic seed=2026, closed-form solvers, zero external dependencies
assumptions_and_limits: Reference implementation for production teams building zero-dependency evaluation harnesses.
